question: For $A=\begin{bmatrix}k&2\\k-1&3\end{bmatrix}$, determine $k$ if $\operatorname{adj}A$ is symmetric. Hence, find $|A|$ for the obtained value and state whether $A$ is nonsingular.
explanation:
Formation of the adjoint
For the given matrix, $$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}3&-2\\1-k&k\end{bmatrix}$$
Symmetry condition
A matrix is symmetric when its corresponding off-diagonal entries are equal. Therefore, $$-2=1-k$$
Determination of the parameter
Solving gives $$k=3$$
Determinant for the obtained value
For $k=3$, $$|A|=\begin{vmatrix}3&2\\2&3\end{vmatrix}=9-4=5$$
Nonsingularity conclusion
Since $|A|=5\ne0$, the matrix $A$ is nonsingular.
